newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares falling on traders' rate hike fears.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares falling on traders' rate hike fears.

text.p: Leading Russian shares fell at the opening on Friday, hit by Moscow traders' worries over what they saw as a possible U.S interest rate hike and tracking falls in European and U.S. markets.
Dealers forecast further easing of less than five percent.
"Russian markets are following Europe and emerging markets on comments by Greenspan," said Boris Shvedsky of Aton.
U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan made comments on Thursday which Russian traders said caused them to think that a 25 basis point short-term interest rate hike was likely.

Many dealers said share prices, which have already slipped as much as 20 percent this month, were nearing support levels, though some added that if expected support did not emerge, a further quick drop could occur.
The Russian Trading System 23-share index had fallen to 312.55 at 0900 GMT from 313.35 at Thursday's close.
UES EESR.RTS national power utility had fallen 20 cents to $0.1960 at 0920 from $0.2040 at Thursday's close. Surgutneftegaz oil company prefs SNGS_p.RTS had dropped to $0.535 from $0.558.
"People are more looking at what is happening in the States," said Peter Kizenko, chief equity dealer at ING Barings.
Kizenko predicted the Moscow Times Index, which closed at 227.46 on Thursday, would find support at 220 and could trade down if support did not appear.
Shvedsky said the RTS index could see another half-percent fall, adding, "shares are still going down, but for some we are seeing the fall slow."

Dan Rapoport, director of institutional sales at CentreInvest, said there was selective buying by Westerners of some leading shares despite the fall. But he predicted a gradual net slip of two percent through the end of the month.
"Volumes are the best indicator," he said. "As long as reported RTS volume is below $40 million the decline will continue."
Volume was a weak $30 million on Thursday and has generally been below $40 million this week.
